text:
Braden Schneider has been a Ranger since going 19th overall in 2020, 368 games and counting. He hits (42 in 18 games), he skates well for his size, and lately he's been playing more, a little over 19 minutes a night across his last ten. He missed practice with an illness at the end of October and was back for the next game.

Not everyone's convinced. With Scott Morrow playing well since getting into the lineup, Blue Line Station argued the Rangers have "no excuse to keep playing Braden Schneider." Our numbers are kinder this season: New York has had 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, a bit better than without him, and the goals have tracked those chances almost exactly.

The longer-term worries are real, though. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating very little offense with him on last season (bottom 1% of defensemen), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found only 30% of his exits kept possession. Two assists in 18 games should rise; our projection has about 16 points the rest of the way.
headline: Braden Schneider's chances look better than his points
